title: Perturbation-based smoke suite for embedding + reranker with explainable regression alerts
creator: Priya Nair
description: Add a lightweight, perturbation-driven smoke test suite that runs automatically whenever embedding or reranker config/model artifacts are updated. The suite focuses on offline recall/precision checks, targeted drift probes, and a small explainability layer that surfaces which perturbations caused failures so SRE/ML engineers can debug quickly.
background: We currently run large offline evals for embedding and reranker changes but those can be slow and are not always triggered for small config tweaks (quantization profile changes, KV cache window, batcher policy). Multiple recent regressions were only discovered in production or during costly manual runs. We need a fast, deterministic smoke layer that gates config/model pushes and gives human-readable signals about why a regression happened.
proposal: 1) Implement a suite that runs on PR/config-change webhook and CI for canary deployments. 2) The suite composes: (A) a compact benchmark set (2k queries) sampled from representative cohorts, (B) perturbation generators (token drop, paraphrase, query length scaling, embedding noise, embedding quantization sim), and (C) metrics + explainability reports that map failing queries to perturbation type and config diff. 3) Expose results to console + rollout gating: if offline_recall@10 drops by >= 2% absolute or if drift metric (cosine mean shift) exceeds threshold for priority cohorts, block canary rollouts and create an auto-annotated incident in the evals dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke suite runs automatically for any model or config PR touching embedding/reranker infra (runtime, quant profiles, cache size, batcher).
False-positive rate on block decisions remains below 5% after two calibration cycles.
Offline recall@10 and precision@10 measured on compact benchmark computed within 12 minutes for canary CI runs.
Explainability report links failing queries to the perturbation that caused degradation in at least 75% of detected regressions.
Console shows a clear pass/warn/fail status and a link to the annotated diff + suggested rollback when fail occurs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): run suite in CI on a subset of teams and post results to a dedicated Slack channel (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (soft block): enable gating for non-critical configs (quantization profile tweaks, cache params) in canary environments with a 24h override policy (3 weeks).
Phase 3 (enforced block): enable gating for all embedding/reranker model and critical config changes; integrate with rollout automation to stop canary->prod promotion on failures (2 weeks).
test_plan: Unit tests for each perturbation generator and for deterministic seed behavior.
End-to-end CI job that runs the suite on a known-good baseline and a synthetic-broken baseline to validate detection and explainability outputs.
A/B test on low-traffic canary fleet to measure real-world false positives and time-to-detect regressions.
Load test to ensure the suite does not exceed CI time budget (target < 12 minutes wall clock).
metrics: mean_cosine_shift_per_cohort - track cohort-level embedding distribution drift
percent_failures_explained - percent of failing queries with an identified perturbation cause
